bug_description.original: A heap buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the H5MM_memcpy function, allowing out-of-bounds write operations.
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness drives matio's MATLAB v7.3 / HDF5 parser into `Mat_H5ReadGroupInfo()` on a group with a `MATLAB_fields` attribute. On that path the caller's `nfields` local starts at 0, and `Mat_H5ReadFieldNames()` asks HDF5 for the attribute dataspace dimensions. For the crashing attribute that dataspace is scalar, so `H5Sget_simple_extent_dims()` reports rank 0 and matio leaves `*nfields` at 0. Vulnerable code then allocates `fieldnames_vl` for zero `hvl_t` entries and passes that buffer to `H5Aread()`. Inside HDF5, the same scalar dataspace still has one element, so `H5A__read()` computes `nelmts = 1` and `H5MM_memcpy()` copies 16 bytes into the zero-element destination. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow write, and the patch fixes this exact mismatch by treating the scalar `err == 0` case as `*nfields = 1` before allocation.

source.description: First project statement that materializes attacker-controlled state used by the overflow. It reads the `MATLAB_fields` attribute dataspace and leaves the caller-provided field-count slot reflecting the scalar-dataspace case that drives the undersized allocation.
source.value_from: In `Mat_H5ReadGroupInfo()` the current group's `nfields` local is initialized to 0 at line 739 and then passed by address into `Mat_H5ReadFieldNames()` when `H5Aexists_by_name(dset_id, ".", "MATLAB_fields", H5P_DEFAULT)` succeeds. The only staged fix is `if (err == 0) *nfields = 1;`, and HDF5's `H5S_get_simple_extent_dims()` comment states that return value 0 means a scalar dataspace. Together with the saved allocation-at-625 and crash-at-626 stack frames, that pins the witnessed path to a scalar `MATLAB_fields` attribute that leaves `*nfields` at 0 here.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Closest project sink. This call hands the zero-element `fieldnames_vl` buffer to HDF5 as the destination for the entire `MATLAB_fields` attribute read.
sink.note: The saved ASan stack shows this frame immediately above `H5A__read` and `H5MM_memcpy`, where the actual 16-byte out-of-bounds write occurs.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The code uses the scalar-rank value left in `*nfields` as an element count and allocates for zero `hvl_t` entries instead of normalizing the scalar case to one field.
root_cause.note: The patch adds the missing obligation immediately before this allocation: if `H5Sget_simple_extent_dims()` returns 0, set `*nfields = 1` before allocating. ASan's allocation stack points to this exact line and reports the resulting heap region as 1 byte wide, consistent with `malloc(0)`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant input is the `MATLAB_fields` attribute dataspace. This statement is where matio first reads that attacker-controlled dataspace into state later used for allocation sizing.

parser_admitted.description: The input has already been admitted as a MATLAB 7.3 / HDF5 structure group, and the presence of `MATLAB_fields` dispatches execution into the vulnerable field-name reader instead of the safe link-iteration fallback.

fine_trace.note: Parser admission. On this group-parsing path `nfields` was initialized to 0 at line 739, and because the attacker-controlled group exposes `MATLAB_fields`, matio passes `&nfields` into `Mat_H5ReadFieldNames()` instead of taking the link-iteration fallback.

Source. This reads the attacker-controlled dataspace of `MATLAB_fields`. For the crashing attribute that dataspace is scalar, so `H5Sget_simple_extent_dims()` reports rank 0; because step 1 supplied a caller slot already holding 0, `*nfields` remains 0 after this call.

Root cause. The code uses the scalar-rank result from step 2 as an allocation count and reserves space for 0 `hvl_t` entries instead of fixing up the scalar case to 1. On the saved run, ASan records this `malloc(0)` as a 1-byte heap region.
Closest project sink. The zero-element destination buffer from step 3 is passed into HDF5 for the full attribute read.
The same scalar attribute dataspace still carries one element in HDF5, so `H5A__read()` derives `nelmts = 1`. This creates the direct mismatch with step 3's zero-entry destination buffer.

With `buf` still pointing at `fieldnames_vl` from step 4 and `nelmts == 1` from step 5, HDF5 issues a copy of one converted attribute element into the zero-entry buffer. On the saved run ASan reports this copy size as 16 bytes.
AddressSanitizer crash site. `dest` is the buffer allocated in step 3 and `n == 16`, so the write starts immediately beyond the 1-byte heap region ASan attributes to `Mat_H5ReadFieldNames:625`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid write lands 0 bytes to the right of the 1-byte region allocated here, consistent with `malloc(0)` for zero `hvl_t` entries.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: closest project sink is `Mat_H5ReadFieldNames:626`; the next saved frames are `H5A__read:658` and `H5MM_memcpy:597` where ASan reports the write

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_58262 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/matio_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 16` in `H5MM_memcpy` with stack `H5A__read -> H5Aread -> Mat_H5ReadFieldNames`.

format.name: MATLAB v7.3 HDF5 file
format.contract: A MATLAB 7.3 / HDF5 input that reaches `Mat_H5ReadGroupInfo()` on a structure group with a `MATLAB_fields` attribute whose dataspace is scalar (rank 0) even though the attribute still carries one variable-length field-name element. In the vulnerable source that exact scalar/one-element mismatch makes `H5Sget_simple_extent_dims()` leave `*nfields == 0`, `malloc((size_t)(*nfields) * sizeof(hvl_t))` allocate zero slots, and `H5Aread()` copy one 16-byte element into that buffer.
